title: CUDA paths under noncontiguous inputs, duplicate observers, repeated calls, released host inputs, a caller stream, cancellation and exceptions

fixture.problem: the G4-02 problem: 20 x 18 x 16 cells, 0.1 um mesh, 4 CPML cells, index-1.5 sphere, Ez point source, Ez point monitor, x-normal plane DFT with three frequencies, float64

checks.noncontiguous_inputs: epsilon as a permuted view of a transposed copy and as a stride-2 slice of a larger tensor, through DifferentiableSimulation forward and backward
checks.noncontiguous_rejection: FusedYeeCUDA on a grid whose E is a transposed view, and _direct_cuda_view on a strided or CPU tensor
checks.duplicate_observers: the point monitor and the plane monitor registered twice under different ids in Simulation (torch/torch/eager and fused/fused/graph); duplicate point monitors in the adjoint with torch and fused backward
checks.repeated_calls: two runs of one Simulation object with the same graph setting and one with the opposite setting; two forward calls of one DifferentiableSimulation, two torch.autograd.grad calls on one graph with retain_graph, one on the other graph, and a .backward accumulation
checks.input_lifetime: the host numpy array and its CPU tensor are deleted after the CUDA upload and confirmed collected by a weak reference before the run
checks.stream_synchronization: the whole run inside torch.cuda.stream(side) for torch/fused kernels with graphs off and on, and the adjoint with torch and fused backward
checks.cancellation: threading.Event set from the first progress callback at step 5; the run must report cancelled at that step
checks.exception: a progress callback that raises RuntimeError at step 5; a backward with create_graph=True which the discrete adjoint refuses
checks.allocator: torch.cuda.memory_allocated() after gc.collect() and torch.cuda.synchronize(), against a baseline taken after one warm-up run of the same configuration

reference_method: self-consistency of the CUDA path: the contiguous, single-observer, first-call, default-stream, uncancelled run of the same discrete problem on the same device; the G4-02 case ties that run to the CPU float64 solution

observables.name: forward identity
observables.definition: numpy.testing.assert_array_equal on E, H, signals, frames, frame steps, plane DFT fields and flux (bitwise)

observables.name: gradient agreement
observables.definition: epsilon gradient against the reference gradient, or against twice it for duplicate observers and accumulation

observables.name: leaked_bytes
observables.definition: torch.cuda.memory_allocated() after cleanup minus the warm baseline

observables.name: termination
observables.definition: summary.termination_reason, summary.cancelled and summary.steps of the cancelled run

acceptance.identity: forward results and adjoint signals are bitwise identical to the reference run; noncontiguous epsilon views give bitwise identical signals and gradients
acceptance.gradients: duplicate-observer, repeated-call, accumulated and side-stream gradients agree with the reference gradient within rtol 1e-7 and atol 1e-9 times max |gradient_ref|

allocator.definition: no torch CUDA bytes remain allocated after a cancelled run or after an exception, relative to the warm baseline

acceptance.cancellation: termination_reason 'cancelled', cancelled true, 0 < steps < 60, exactly one progress event at the cancelled step, signals truncated to that step
acceptance.rejection_policy: numpy input, float16, complex, mismatched precision, wrong shape, epsilon < 1, NaN, a string cuda_graph_steps and an unknown checkpoint storage each raise ValueError with the named message; noncontiguous fused-kernel grid arrays raise ValueError 'Fused CUDA arrays must be contiguous'; strided or CPU tensors raise ValueError 'Direct CUDA views require contiguous'
acceptance.source_of_limits: completion_gates.json proposed_thresholds discrete_dimensionless_fp64; the allocator tolerance of zero bytes and the bitwise identities are fixture-specific budgets declared here before the run

not_yet_covered: the same checks on a second CUDA platform (RTX 5880 Ada): prepared, not run here

notes: Runs on the shared RTX 3060 with a 5760-cell grid. memory_allocated counts torch allocations only; CuPy holds no device memory for these kernels beyond compiled modules, which are not allocator bytes.
